run.cache: cold = a fresh browser context with Network.clearBrowserCache before the navigation; warm = the same context and page as the cold landing, reloaded with its cache kept
run.classification: Each resource is classified by file extension first (js/mjs = script, css = stylesheet, woff/woff2/ttf/otf/eot = font, png/jpg/jpeg/webp/avif/gif/svg/ico/bmp = image), then by initiatorType (script, img/image, fetch/xmlhttprequest), and everything else is other.
run.signIn: POST /api/auth/login through the browser context's request client (not a page visit), so no app asset was fetched into the cache before the measured navigation

scenarios.label: landing → chat client-side transition (a conversation clicked on /)

cache.detail: fresh browser context, cleared cache, then the landing document; the conversation was clicked on that page (the chat route's chunks were not in the cache)

scenarios.paintsNote: a client-side navigation creates no new document, navigation timing entry or paint entry; the landing document's FCP/LCP/DCL/load are in landingDocument

usable.method: the chat link was clicked, then the chat surface and the composer were waited for and the composer was clicked; usableAtMs minus clickedAtMs is the transition's usable time
usable.clickMethod: locator.click() on the conversation link, then on the composer
usable.caveat: the composer is the same test id on both pages; the chat surface's arrival and the URL change are recorded too, so the shared-control caveat is visible in the numbers

notes: the landing document before the click was measured the same way as the cold landing scenario; its numbers are in landingDocument, not in this scenario's navigation/paints
